transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I guess what brings me in is that... I just don't feel real happiness or closeness to anyone anymore. 

It's hard to explain, but even when my wife tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or if something at work goes really well, I just can't feel it. I don't feel anything good.
Do you ever feel detached from yourself or as though the world around you is unreal?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean... I know who I am, and everything around me feels real enough. It's not like I feel like I'm outside my body or that things seem fake. I'm definitely here. It's just... I just don't really have any reaction to what's going on around me anymore.
How long has this lack of happiness been going on?
It started about a year and seven months ago. Ever since the retrofit accident, really. That's when all this began.
Since this began, has your loss of pleasure been present continuously, without a period of at least two months when you felt back to your usual self?

Yeah, it's been continuous. I definitely haven't had any period where I felt back to my usual self, let alone for a stretch of two months. It's just been a constant thing every day since the accident.
Besides the loss of pleasure, have you felt sad, down, or empty most of the day on most days?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. It's not like I'm walking around feeling miserable or crying or anything like that. I just... I just don't really feel much of anything. Like I said, it's more of a flat feeling than actually being sad.
Are the consequences of the retrofit accident still affecting your life now?

Yeah, they definitely are. At work, I've actually had to hand off a lot of the floor responsibilities that I used to manage myself. I just... I can't do it right now. And recently I had an interview for a regional director position, and I lost my composure so badly that I actually just walked out of the room. 

And it's not just work. At home, my marriage feels really strained. I'm there physically, you know, in the house, but I'm not really participating in our life together anymore. So, yeah, it's impacting pretty much everything.
Since the accident, have you noticed any significant change in your sleep?

Yeah, it's definitely changed. Most nights I just lie there, you know, replaying the plant in my head. And when I actually do manage to sleep, I either jolt awake from dreams about the line, or... or I just wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning. Either way, I always wake up feeling like I never rested at all.
Do you find yourself avoiding people, places, activities, or conversations that remind you of the retrofit accident?

Yeah, I do. I avoid that specific production line whenever I can. If it needs to be walked or checked on, I'll just send someone else to do it. And... if people start talking about the rollout or the investigation into what happened, I just shut the conversation down. I don't want to talk about it or be around it.
Have these trauma-related symptoms continued for more than three months?
Yeah, definitely more than three months. It's... well, this has all been going on ever since the retrofit accident. So that makes it about a year and seven months ago now.
